AMANDA · RELATIONSHIP MANAGER

        
Execute the daily RM workflow

        
Start in Today. Work the priority the tracker gives you, log activity as you go, prospect for new meetings, manage your assigned portfolio, and keep follow-ups/current relationships moving.

        
Planning target: 30+ partner meetings/month, initially about 10 new + 20 existing.

What counts as a partner meeting?

    
Counts: New Realtor Meeting, existing/current Partner Meeting, Break Bread / Face Time, Strategic Partner Meeting, Channel Meeting, Team / Office Presentation, and Retention / At-Risk Meeting when they are real partner-facing meetings.

    
Does not count toward the partner-meeting goal: Amanda coaching/development, RM scorecard review, portfolio review, process improvement, tracker/system development, RM training, or internal leadership/escalation support.


    
AUTO PLAN in Management View: tracker-generated relationship/leadership suggestions that fit around Nyny’s real schedule blocks. They are not calendar meetings and not logged activity until the work is actually completed and logged.

    
Simple rule: Amanda works from Today. Nyny works from Management View. Both keep the relationship truth clean in Portfolio + Activity History.

Partner Check-In — Don’t Waste the Touch

    
A real partner conversation should leave us knowing more than “they’re doing good.” Capture what matters while it’s fresh. These answers update Portfolio + Partner Health.

    

    

      Use these naturally — not like an interview.

      “What are you focused on right now / what’s coming up?”

      “Anything making business harder or anything we could do better?”

      “Are we getting most of your lending opportunities, or are some going elsewhere?”

      “What’s the best next move for us to help you?”

Activity Guide

    
The role comes down to two things: bring in new agents, and keep the agents we have engaged and getting value from us. Every activity type below fits into one of those two buckets. Use this anytime you're not sure what to log something as.

    

      If you're mid-call and not sure which type fits, log your best guess and keep going, don't stop the conversation to check this guide. You can always fix it after: open Activity Feed, find the entry, hit Edit.
    


    

      Quick note on "Agent Talk-to's" Every touch should leave the agent with something of value: a market insight, useful feedback, a resource, a pipeline review, a file update, a genuine check-in on how their business is going. Think account executive: proactive, consultative, and always bringing something of value. It's what keeps you top-of-mind so agents think of NFM first.
    


    
1 · New Business (Growth) 🌱

    
Agents you've never worked with before. These don't count toward your Talk-to goal; they've got their own goals to hit.

    

      
Cold CallsYour very first reach-out to someone new, not in the book yet. If you've talked to them before, even once, it's not cold anymore.

      
New Realtor MeetingThe first real sit-down: go over standards of service and ask for the opportunity to earn their business. First meetings should be coffee or in-office — office tour, meet the team, go over what we offer. Save lunch for break breads with agents you already have a relationship with.

    


    
2 · Get the Opportunity 🚀

    
That first meeting isn't the finish line; they're not really on board until they send us a lead. Getting them set up on the tools is what makes that first lead possible, so keep following up until it happens.

    

      
New Agent Follow-up counts as Talk-toChecking in and helping a newly met agent get set up on HomeBot, ListReports, and Total Expert, moving them toward that first lead.

      
Onboarding checklistThe 7 quick tasks (Retained Report, Sa Team email, HomeBot, ListReports, Total Expert, group text, asking for the opportunity + referral language + LP CC'd). Complete these the same day as the meeting.

      
Gifting campaignEvery agent in this program needs a call once a week for their first 4 weeks. This is one of the most important parts of the role. Tracked on Snapshot, which follows the 4-Week Conversion Skillset: break the ice, a value touch, an opportunity call, then accountability follow-up.

    


    
3 · If They Go Quiet: Reconnect 🔁

    
If an agent hasn't sent us a lead in 90 days, they fall off and land on the Reconnect list (its own tab). That's a flag that it's time to work on earning a lead from them again. Re-engaging someone from that list is not a Cold Call: the relationship already exists, you're just picking it back up. Log it as Reconnect Outreach, not a regular Agent Talk-to, since technically they're not active until they send a lead again. It still counts toward your Talk-to goal.


    
4 · Staying in Touch 💛

    
Everything marked counts as Talk-to feeds into your weekly Talk-to goal (100/week). Log it once and it does double duty. Whatever the reason for the touch, use it to get real feedback on how the relationship is going. Every touch is an opportunity.

    

      
Agent Talk-to counts as Talk-toA proactive check-in with an agent who's currently active and sending business.

      
Reconnect Outreach counts as Talk-toThe right type for re-engaging someone from the Reconnect list. It's not a Cold Call since you already know them, but a regular Agent Talk-to isn't quite right either since they haven't sent a lead in 90+ days.

      
CTC Call counts as Talk-toProcess: call the agent, leave a voicemail if no answer, then follow up with a text. Script is in Scripts + Training. Get feedback from both the buyer's agent and the listing agent. Share that feedback on WhatsApp with the team in real-time, proactively, the way Daniel does, proactively. Check Encompass for the CTC milestone  Always ask the listing agent for a meeting if they don't already work with us; a closing is a natural door-opener. If there's a closing issue or poor feedback, set the outcome to "Needs manager attention" so it surfaces for the team.

      
Under Contract Call counts as Talk-to, note requiredFirst call to the listing agent as soon as a deal you're the buyer's lender on goes under contract. Script is in Scripts + Training.

      
Birthday / Holiday Outreach counts as Talk-toA personal touch: wish the agent a happy birthday or happy holidays. When the birthday alert shows on Snapshot, send a text, give a quick call, or both. If the agent is a top producer, let the team know so they can wish them well too. When you are on a call with any agent, check if their birthday is on file — a lot of data is missing. If you do not have it, ask and add it to their contact so you never miss it.

      
Agent Appreciation counts as Talk-toRecognizing a top producer or celebrating a milestone.

      
Market Update counts as Talk-toSharing what's happening in the market: inventory, days on market, buyer demand, listing trends. This isn't financing or rates; that stays with the LP team.

      
Break Breads note required, 10+ wordsMore than a meal: sitting down with the agent to get real feedback and confirm the relationship is genuinely solid. Its own goal (5/week), separate from Talk-to's. To figure out who's due, check the Break Bread Due List on Snapshot (or the Face Time Tracker on the LP tracker), it shows last touch date per agent across both you and the LPs. Consider bringing the assigned LP along when it makes sense.

      
Realtor Buddy Referral AskAsk an existing happy agent to introduce you to someone else they know. Log the ask when you make it; do not create a follow-up obligation for that agent. Outcome goal: 3 actual buddy introductions received per week. When an intro arrives, use “Buddy intro received” so the result is tracked separately from the ask.

      
Co-hosted EventHosting something together with the agent.

      
Team / Office PresentationA presentation or relationship meeting with a Realtor team, brokerage, builder office, or partner group. Count the event once as one partner meeting regardless of how many people attend; it does not count as multiple New Realtor Meetings.

    


    
Still not sure? Just ask.


    
  






  

    
Agent Strategy

    
Skillset Training: talking points and frameworks for actual agent conversations.


    
The How to Refer System

    
Don't just ask for leads. Install the referral language. The agent needs the exact text, email path, and buyer expectations, not a vague ask.

    

      Agent uses the exact script at the first buyer interaction → Buyer expects a lender call within hours → Lender receives name, phone, email, goals, timing, and obstacles.
    

    

      Coach this line after sending the guide: "This is the exact language I recommend using whenever a buyer mentions they may purchase."
    


    
Coach Agents to Refer Earlier

    
Earlier introductions create more control and more conversion. Don't wait until the buyer is ready to tour homes.

    

      
Early = plan + education + excitement + lender preference

      
Late = rate comparison + urgency + weaker influence

    


    
Existing Partner Lead Growth Framework

    
Earn more share by tying support to the agent's goals. The ask doesn't feel like begging when it follows value, feedback, and accountability.

    

      
1. State the goal"I want to earn all of your business."

      
2. Ask for feedback"What can I improve to earn more?"

      
3. Learn their goalsTransactions, pipeline, stuck buyers.

      
4. Offer a specific actionReview stalled buyers, events, intros.

      
5. Ask for greater opportunityEarlier intros, larger lead share.

    

    

      Core question: "What can I improve to earn more of your business?"
    


    
Relationship Builder vs. Transactional Lender

    
Deep relationships reduce partner turnover. Business relationships are replaceable; personal loyalty is harder to displace.

    

      
Transactional lender: calls only when there's a deal, sends generic marketing, asks for leads, disappears after closing.

      
Relationship builder: builds a personal cadence, creates value, helps the agent hit goals, puts the agent first.

    

    
Relationship actions: relevant humor, family milestones, events with partners, agent introductions.

Partner Health — What It Means

    
Partner Health is now an action signal, not just a report. Red and Yellow partners feed the daily Workflow so the portfolio gets worked before relationships quietly slip.

    

      
Green
Relationship is on cadence, recent business is healthy, and there is no active competitor-risk flag. Maintain the normal relationship plan.

      
Yellow
A warning signal: business or meaningful contact is getting stale. Reconnect, identify what changed, document the next growth move, and schedule the next meaningful touch.

      
Red
Needs action now: major lapse in business/contact cadence or competitor risk. Make a meaningful relationship move, document what is happening, and escalate when needed.

    

    
Daily priority: urgent escalation → must-do transaction calls → Red Partner Health → overdue follow-ups → Yellow Partner Health / relationship work → new-agent calls.

    
Health is calculated from recent lead activity, meaningful relationship contact, tier cadence, and competitor-risk signals. Click any Partner Health tile in Portfolio Review to see the actual names.

Cold Call — Opening Script

    
Before you dial: Pull up RETR and look them up. Find a recent sale or listing and mention it in your opener — "I saw your listing at [address] just closed, congrats!" It makes the call personal and shows you did your homework.

    
Goal: introduce yourself, explain how we support agents, and schedule a 20-minute meeting.

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], I wanted to reach out and introduce myself. We love working alongside agents to help buyers better understand their financing options, create listing-specific payment strategies, and explore creative financing options to help ensure you and your clients are winning in this market. I would love to learn more about your business and explore ways we can support you. Would you be open to a quick 20-minute meeting sometime next week?"
    

    
When scheduling — offer two options:

    

      "Would Tuesday at 11:00 or Thursday at 2:00 work better for you?"
    


    
Cold Call — Common Responses

    

      
What's the meeting about?"We'd love to learn more about the clients and areas you serve, what you're currently focused on growing, and where additional lending support may be helpful. We can also share some of the financing strategies and listing resources we provide to our agent partners."

      
Already have a lender"That's completely understandable, and we're not asking you to replace a relationship that's working well. We'd simply love the opportunity to introduce ourselves and become an additional resource when you need a second opinion, have a challenging scenario, or need extra support. Would you still be open to a 20-minute meeting?"

      
Send me some info"Absolutely. I want to make sure I send something relevant. Would buyer financing options, listing-specific payment strategies, or solutions for more challenging scenarios be most helpful? I'll send that over today. Would it be okay if I follow up with you on [day]?"

      
I'm busy right now"No problem at all, I completely understand. Would there be a better time for me to call you back, or would it be easier if I sent you a quick text?"

      
Not interested"I completely understand. Thank you for taking my call. I'll send you my contact information in case you ever need an additional lending resource or a second opinion on a scenario."

    


    
No Answer — Follow-Up Text

    
Send immediately after the missed call.

    

      "Hey [Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I just tried to give you a quick call to introduce myself. We love working alongside agents to support their buyers, create listing-specific payment strategies, and explore creative financing options to help you and your clients win in this market. I would love to connect for a quick 20-minute conversation. Do you have any availability next week?"
    


    

      Practice note from leadership: These scripts, objection handling, and value proposition scenarios live here in Skillset Training. Practice for 10 minutes before starting new-agent calls and use the talk tracks during live work.
    



      

    

    

      
        Transaction CallsUnder-contract and CTC calls for buyer and listing agents.
        ＋
      
      

    

      
Listing Agent Conversion Playbook

      
Turn a smooth transaction into a retained Realtor meeting

      
The listing agent is one of the warmest new relationships available: there is already a transaction, a reason to call, and several moments to demonstrate value. The goal is not a pitch at closing. The goal is to ask early, deliver what matters, then collect the meeting you earned.

      

        
1 · CHECK
Run the active-agent search first. If they already work with an NFM LO, protect that relationship and simply execute a great file.

        
2 · ASK EARLY
Use the intro call to learn how they want the transaction handled and earn a conditional 15-minute meeting.

        
3 · DELIVER
Be the person who calls with the appraisal-at-value and clear-to-close good news.

        
4 · COLLECT
At CTC, remind them you delivered and put the retained Realtor meeting on the calendar.

      

      
Do not lose the team behind the agent: capture the transaction coordinator and anyone else who should receive updates in Encompass. Their experience can strengthen or kill the relationship.

    

    
Under Contract Call (Listing Agent)

    
Call the listing agent as soon as a deal you're the buyer's lender on goes under contract. Set the tone early, this is your first real touchpoint with them on this file.

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] from the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I'm calling about your listing at [Property Address], which has just gone into contract. I'm the lender representing the buyer. First, I have a couple of questions about the transaction, I want to make sure we have a smooth process. Does that sound good? Congratulations again on the sale."
    

    
Discovery questions to cover:

    
    
      
  • Will this be a remote, mail-away, POA, or otherwise non-standard closing?
    • 
      
  • What is your preferred communication method: call, text, or email?
    • 
      
  • Which milestones do you specifically want us to update you on?
    • 
      
  • Is there anything about the file you are concerned about or want us watching closely?
    • 
      
  • Is the seller relying on these proceeds for a simultaneous or next-home closing?
    • 
      
  • Who else on your team, including a transaction coordinator, should we keep informed?
    • 
    

    

      "Our team is available nights and weekends, so I'm going to send you a quick text with my contact info. Please don't hesitate to reach out anytime if you or your seller need anything."
    

    
Commitment close — ask on the introductory call:

    

      "If we can deliver a smooth transaction and have the loan clear to close at least three days before closing, can I earn 15 minutes of your time to talk about how we might grow our businesses together?"
    

    
After the call: save the transaction coordinator/other team contacts in Encompass, send a separate digital business card/contact card, document their communication preferences and concerns, and log the Under Contract Call. The appraisal-at-value and CTC are your two highest-leverage direct-call moments — do not let automation be the only messenger.


    
Under Contract Call (Buyer's Agent)

    
Call the buyer's agent once the file goes under contract. This call sets the tone for how you will work together throughout.

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] from the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I'm calling about [Buyer Name]'s contract on [Property Address] — congratulations to you and your buyers for going into contract! I wanted to reach out personally and introduce myself. [LP Name] will be your main point of contact throughout the transaction and our team is here to support you every step of the way."
    

    
Questions to cover:

    
    
      
  • Are there any concerns or anything we should know going in?
    • 
      
  • What's the best way to keep you updated throughout the process — text, email, calls?
    • 
      
  • Regarding the closing date — we want to make sure we stick with the contracted date. We do not move up closing dates. Once we are clear to close, if all parties are in agreement we can revisit at that point.
    • 
    

    

      "Our team is available nights and weekends, so I'm going to send you a quick text with my contact info. Please reach out anytime. We are going to take good care of your buyer."
    

    
If they don't already work with us regularly, close for a meeting before ending the call: "I'd love to sit down sometime, even just 15 minutes, to see if it makes sense to work together."

    
After the call, send a follow-up text with your contact info. Log this as an Under Contract Call — it counts as a Talk-to.


    
CTC Call

    
Process: call the agent, leave a voicemail if no answer, follow up with a text if still no response.

    

      "Hi [Agent Name], this is [Your Name], I'm the Relationship Manager for the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. Congrats on getting [Buyer/Property] to clear to close! I wanted to check in personally, was there anything that went really smoothly for you, or anything we could've done better on our end?"
    

    
For the listing agent, use CTC to collect the meeting you earned. If they agreed to the commitment close earlier, remind them that the team delivered and put the 15 minutes on the calendar. If they do not answer, leave a voicemail that asks for a callback rather than only sending an FYI text.

    

      "We delivered what we promised and we're clear to close. I'd love to collect those 15 minutes we talked about — does [day/time] or [day/time] work better?"

      Gifting Campaign Scripts (4-Week Cadence)
Always try a call first. If no answer, follow up with a text.
    


    
Week 1: Break the Ice

    
Call:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I wanted to follow up after our meeting. It was great connecting with you and I'm excited to work together. How has your week been going?"
    

    
Text if no answer:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], this is [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. Great meeting with you. Looking forward to working together. Here to support you and your buyers."
    


    
Week 2: Value Touch

    
Call:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. I've been thinking about your business and wanted to share something I think will be useful for you. [share resource or market update]. Would you have a few minutes this week to connect?"
    

    
Text if no answer:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. I have something I think will be useful for you. [resource]. Let's connect this week!"
    


    
Week 3: Opportunity Call

    
Call:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. I've really enjoyed getting to know you. Do you have any buyers right now we can help with? We would love to earn your business."
    

    
Text if no answer:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. Do you have any buyers we can help with right now? We would love to earn your business."
    


    
Week 4: Accountability Follow-Up

    
Call:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM. Wanted to connect and see how your business is going. Do you have any buyers or listings we can support? We are committed to being your go-to team and we are here whenever you need us."
    

    
Text if no answer:

    

      "Hey [Agent Name], it's [Your Name] with NFM. Do you have any buyers or listings we can support right now? We are here whenever you need us."
    


    

      Note: Replace [resource or market update] in Week 2 with something specific to that agent. The more relevant it is to their market or situation, the better it lands.
    


    
New Agent Meeting — Commitment & 4-Week Follow-Up

    
The most common failure mode: great meeting, agent signs up for the mailing list, nothing else happens. This framework closes that gap. The commitment ask is the single most important moment — get it every time, no exceptions.


    
The Commitment Ask — end of every new agent meeting

    

      "Do I have your commitment to send me the next two to three leads that come your way?"
    

    

      Deliver this while looking them in the eye and shaking their hand. This creates a spoken agreement that is genuinely difficult to break without consciously going back on their word. Ending a meeting with a vague "let me know if I can ever help" puts zero pressure on the agent and gives you no leverage to follow up on. The handshake is what makes weeks 3 and 4 feel earned rather than pushy. Getting a lead within the first 30 days is critical — after that window closes, the agent has usually reverted to their previous lender and reconverting them becomes exponentially harder.
    


    
The 4-Week Follow-Up Structure


    
Week 0 — Day of the meeting

    
Send the How to Refer template (see script above). Add them on social media. No ask yet — this is pure value delivery.


    
Week 1 — Break the walls down

    
Send a relatable meme or short video — nothing salesy. Just staying on their radar in a human way.

    
No direct ask. Goal is to make them smile and remember you.


    
Week 2 — Value touch, still no ask

    
Send something relevant — mailing campaign content, a market update, or something from the sales meeting. Nothing that asks for a lead.

    
Patience here pays off in week 3. Two touches in, no pressure — this is what separates you from the LO who emailed them three times in a row asking for business.


    
Week 3 — First lead ask, paired with a unique product

    

      "Hey [Agent], I was thinking about you — do you have any buyers who've been told no elsewhere? We have a 1099 program / bank statement option / portfolio loan that might be worth a look. Also, did anyone come to mind since we met that I could help with?"
    

    

      Lead with the unfamiliar product, not a well-known one. Every agent has heard of bank statement and DSCR — leading with something more unique (1099, portfolio program) signals you have tools others don't and gives them a specific reason to think of a client. This activates a specific memory rather than asking them to generate one from nothing.
    


    
Week 4 — Accountability call

    

      "Hey [Agent], I wanted to circle back — when we met, you committed to sending me the next couple of leads that came your way. Is there anyone you're working with right now I could help with?"
    

    
If they push back or go quiet:

    

      "Did I do something wrong?"
    

    

      This surfaces the real reason almost every time — and gives you a chance to fix it, or pivot: "No worries at all — would you be open to just introducing me to whoever you're currently working with? I'd love the chance to earn a second opinion." Either way, you get information you'd never get by staying silent.

For Existing Partners — shifting from earning a lead to earning 100%

    

      "What's one thing we could do better to make working together easier for you?"
    

    
This ask invites specific, actionable feedback and deepens trust simultaneously. The agent who answers this honestly is the one you're going to earn 100% of business from.


    
Pre-Approval Pipeline Playbook

    
When lead volume slows, the first lever is not always more leads — it is converting more of the pre-approved buyers already in the pipeline. Every follow-up should create an opportunity instead of repeating “how's the search going?”

    

      
Week 1
Call: questions about the strategy/programs reviewed; identify anything that changed.

      
Weeks 2–3
Text around actual showings/properties and offer a payment scenario.

      
Week 4
Deliberate break to avoid contact fatigue.

      
Weeks 5–8
Repeat the purposeful cycle, then shift to a 60-day re-engagement cadence.

    

    
Opportunity-creation question when price is the issue:

    
"Is there a property that caught your eye but might be a little more than what you wanted to spend?"

    
Realtor pipeline review — ask these five questions for each buyer:

    
  1. Are they actively looking?
  2. Do they have showings this week?
  3. Have they gone stalled or quiet?
  4. What is preventing movement?
  5. What is the next action and who owns it?

    
Buyer changed Realtors? Move immediately: send the new agent an updated pre-approval letter with highlights, call to introduce yourself and offer help, then create a three-way text with the buyer and new agent. This is a warm new-agent conversion opportunity.

    
Operational foundation: make sure the Pre-Approved Buyer box is checked in Encompass so the pipeline can be pulled by Realtor and the correct Total Expert journey can run.

Core Skillset Practice

      
The live scripts now live in the sections above so there is only one approved version of each talk track. Use this section for practice, not a second copy of the scripts.

      
  • Practice the opener, one objection, and one direct meeting ask for 10 minutes before outbound work.
  • Use a specific next step and two time options instead of “let me know.”
  • Stay confident and relaxed; do not oversell or argue with an existing lender relationship.
  • Document the next action immediately after the conversation.
  • Review one missed conversion opportunity each week and decide what you will do differently next time.

    



      

    

    
  






  

    
Daily Schedule

    

      
Your Role

      
Relationship Manager — Daniel Sa Team, NFM Lending

      
Responsible for growing the team's active agent count and keeping those relationships producing. An active agent is one who has sent us a lead — agents who haven't sent a lead within 90 days fall off the active list and move to the Reconnect queue. Two core responsibilities: bring in new agents through cold calling, outreach, and meetings; and retain the agents we have through consistent, value-driven contact, feedback, and follow-through so they keep referring their clients.

    

    
Working from home: The expectation is that you are actively working your full hours, on Teams, and responsive. If something comes up and you are not able to work, please take PTO or come into the office. WFH is a privilege and the standard is the same as being in office.

    
Default structure for the day. Shifts around actual agent meetings and call-backs. If an agent reaches out outside a planned block, take it, log it, and pick up the block afterward.

    

      
9:00 AMStart of shift. Hours are 9 to 5. If running late, let your manager know.

      
9:15 AMIn office, on Teams, focused, notes ready.

      
10:00–10:30 AMCold call block 1 (~12–13 calls). Two shorter blocks keeps quality up over one long sitting.

      
Tue 10:30Pipeline call.

      
Mon 11:15–12:00Mandatory sales call.

      
12:00–12:30 PMLunch. Goal is to schedule a realtor lunch daily if possible — ideally a break bread with an active or prospective agent. First meetings should be coffee or in-office (office tour, meet the team, go over standards of service) rather than lunch.

      
12:30–1:00 PMCold call block 2 (~12–13 calls).

      
Tue 1:00Level 10 training.

      
Mon 2:30–3:30Skillset.

      
Before calls, daily10 minutes of script and objection practice before starting new-agent calls. Use the live scripts in Skillset Training.

      
4:00–4:30, weekly30-minute 1:1 with your manager once a week. Review the week, cover any questions, work through anything that needs attention. Other days, use this time for self-directed practice or follow-ups.

      
4:45 PM, daily5-minute check-in with your manager, in person or on Teams. Go over the day, make sure we are on track, cover any questions or agent feedback. Followed by a brief email recap.

    

    
  






  

    
Encompass Cheat Guide

    
You don't need to know how to process a file. You need to know where to look when you're talking to an agent. Before every call, have three things open: RETR (to reference their recent sales), Encompass (to check file status), and the team inbox (to catch any recent updates).


    
Milestones — what each one means

    

      
StartedApplication has been taken. File is open and still with the sales team.

      
ProcessingFile is with the loan manager for review. Being prepared for submittal to underwriting.

      
SubmittalLoan has been submitted to underwriting for initial review.

      
ApprovalUnderwriting has reviewed and approved. There may still be conditions to satisfy — check the Conditions tab for what's outstanding.

      
ResubSubmitted to underwriting for final review. Normal and expected — doesn't mean something went wrong. If an agent asks why, tell them it's a standard step in the review process.

      
Clear to Close (CTC)All conditions met. Ready to schedule closing. Your trigger for a CTC call to both agents.

      
Received by CloserClosing docs are with the title/closing company. Closing is imminent.

      
Docs SigningClosing docs are out to title. Borrower is signing.

    


    
Conditions — what they mean

    

      
Prior to DocsMust be satisfied before closing docs can be sent. File cannot move forward until these are cleared.

      
Prior to FundingMust be cleared before funds are released. Closing can happen but money doesn't move until these are done.

    


    
Rate lock

    
Find the lock status and expiration date in the loan file under Rate Lock or Pricing. If a lock is expiring soon and the file isn't close to closing, flag it to the LP. Rate conversations stay with the LP team.


    
Where to find things mid-call

    

      
Current milestonePipeline view — the status column next to the file. Check before every call.

      
Closing dateTop of the loan file in property and closing details. Check if it matches the contract date — if they don't align, mention it to the LP.

      
Outstanding conditionsConditions tab. Shows what's still needed and whether it's prior to docs or prior to funding.

      
Assigned LP / ProcessorFile summary under team members. If you need to escalate, this tells you who to go to.

      
Buyer infoBorrower summary tab — name, contact, employment, loan amount.

      
Rate lock statusRate Lock or Pricing section. Locked vs. floating, and expiration date.

    


    
Attend the weekly pipeline call every Tuesday at 10:30am. This is where you'll hear what's moving, what's stalled, and what agents may need a touch on. It's one of the best ways to stay ahead of conversations before agents call you.

    
If an agent asks something you can't answer with confidence, it's always fine to say "Let me look into that and get back to you shortly" — then actually follow up. Never guess on a file detail.


    
  






  

    
Resources

    
These tools exist to help you find answers quickly and show up prepared. The more you use them, the more confident you'll sound in the field.


    

      
RETRAgent and brokerage lookup — and your secret weapon before every cold call and reconnect. Pull up their profile before you dial: see their recent sales, current listings, and brokerage. Congratulating them on a specific recent sale ("I saw your listing at 123 Main just closed — congrats!") turns a cold call into a warm one instantly.

      
NFM ChatGPTGreat for drafting, quick explanations, and thinking through how to handle a conversation. Use it before, during, or after calls.

      
All RegsNFM's underwriting guidelines. A solid resource when you want to understand what's possible for a buyer before the conversation goes further.

      
EncompassFile status, milestones, conditions, closing dates. Have it open before agent calls. See the Encompass Cheat Guide for where to find specific things.

      
Team inboxHave it open and searchable before calls. If an agent asks about something specific on a file, you can pull the relevant email thread in real time in real time.

      
VelocifyCRM where leads are added and tracked. When an agent refers a buyer, this is where the lead lives. Have it open so you can see what's been referred and by whom.

    


    
The more familiar these tools become, the more confident you'll sound in the field. When you do need to bring something to the team, coming in with what you already found makes the conversation faster and makes the conversation more productive for everyone.
